scope: A stored analysis whose snapshot or trace no longer validates is marked failed and kept aside, so it no longer stops the Worker or blocks queued analyses.
database: A temporary PostgreSQL 14.15 cluster on 127.0.0.1:55432 with a database named issuelens_test. The project cluster on port 5432 was not stopped or modified.
providers: The Worker test used a simulated agent run; no model or GitHub request was made.

reproduction_before_fix.unreadable_queued_row: A queued row with an invalid created_at and trace stopped the Worker with StorageError ('PostgreSQL storage is unavailable'), so the analysis queued after it never ran.
reproduction_before_fix.unreadable_interrupted_row: A running row without a checkpoint and with an incomplete snapshot made the Worker fail at startup.

after_fix.unreadable_queued_row: The row became failed with the incompatible-record error, kept its canonical issue URL and owner, and got a readable trace with stop_reason record_incompatible. The analysis queued after it completed, and the Worker kept running without a reconnect.
after_fix.original_kept: incompatible_record held the original snapshot and trace exactly as stored.
after_fix.unreadable_interrupted_row: Worker startup marked the row failed and opened normally. Without a readable issue URL, the retired snapshot used an empty one.
after_fix.unreadable_fields: Non-object snapshots, non-GitHub URLs, timestamps without a time zone and non-string values fell back to an empty URL and the current UTC time.

limitations: Only rows the Worker claims or recovers are handled. An API read of an unreadable row that the Worker has not reached still returns 503.
The retired snapshot does not carry the old Activity; the original events are kept in incompatible_record.
GitHub text containing a NUL character is still rejected by PostgreSQL JSONB and stops the Worker.
